findings: Oracle memory produced a 41.18 percentage-point absolute uplift over unchanged V2, so structured relevant memory materially helps response quality.

The unchanged V2 bottleneck is mostly upstream of generation: 13 of 17 memory-required queries were classified as retrieval gaps, three as formation or admission gaps, and only one reached the response boundary.

Perfect retrieval is insufficient by itself: the oracle still failed five rubrics because the response prompt forces questions, leaves user-versus-assistant attribute binding ambiguous, underspecifies sensitive abstention wording, or permits incomplete timelines.

Recent-turn selection broke a pronoun follow-up by retaining the assistant acknowledgement while dropping the user turn that contained the answer; recency windows must preserve semantically dependent user-assistant pairs.

The model fabricated state when memory was absent, including no-change assertions, a pending scholarship result, a technical vehicle issue, credential storage locations, and a possible live-data capability. Negative evidence and explicit abstention moves need first-class prompt treatment.
Fifteen of 51 responses were entirely Roman script despite a Devanagari system policy. This is a response-policy compliance problem, not a memory-schema problem.
